marking_schemes.question_text: Explain the term: Photolysis

marking_schemes.question_text: Explain the term Photosynthesis.

marking_schemes.model_answer: When leaf A is tested with iodine solution, it does not turn blue-black; it remains pale/colourless, showing that no starch was formed, since carbon dioxide (absorbed by KOH) was unavailable for photosynthesis.

Each cell type must be clearly drawn and labelled.
common_errors: Omitting platelets; mislabelling granulocyte nuclei shapes

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the biological reason: It is advisable to keep green plants in an aquarium.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the biological reason: Water pollution is a major cause of concern in our country.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the biological reason: We cannot distinguish colours in dim light.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 1 mark for correctly linking colour vision to cone cells and their inactivity in dim light.
key_points: Colour vision is controlled by cone cells, which are not stimulated/activated in dim light; only rod cells (which cannot distinguish colour) function in dim light
marking_schemes.model_answer: Colour vision is controlled by the cone cells of the retina, which require bright light to be stimulated. In dim light, only the rod cells (which cannot distinguish colour) are active, so we cannot distinguish colours.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the biological reason: Medical discoveries such as antibiotics and vaccinations have indirectly contributed to the sharp rise in human population.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 1 mark for correctly linking reduced death rate to population rise.
key_points: Antibiotics and vaccinations have controlled infectious diseases and reduced the death rate, allowing more people to survive, which has led to a sharp rise in population
marking_schemes.model_answer: Antibiotics and vaccinations help control and prevent infectious diseases, which has sharply reduced the death rate. With more people surviving, the population has risen sharply.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the biological reason: Homo sapiens sapiens is the most highly evolved form of man.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 1 mark for correctly linking brain size/intelligence and associated traits to evolutionary status.

marking_schemes.model_answer: Homo sapiens sapiens has a much larger brain in proportion to body size compared to earlier hominids. This is associated with a higher level of intelligence and behavioural traits such as tool use and communication through language, making it the most highly evolved form of man.

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Transpiration and Guttation on the basis of place of occurrence.

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Population control and Swachh Bharat Abhiyan on the basis of one objective.

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Osmosis and Active Transport on the basis of substances undergoing movement.

marking_schemes.model_answer: Osmosis involves the movement of water molecules across a semi-permeable membrane from a region of higher to lower water concentration, whereas active transport involves the movement of solutes (ions/molecules) against their concentration gradient, using metabolic energy (ATP).

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Metaphase and Anaphase on the basis of position of chromosomes.

key_points: In metaphase, chromosomes are arranged at the equatorial plane; in anaphase, sister chromatids/daughter chromosomes separate and move towards opposite poles
marking_schemes.model_answer: In metaphase, chromosomes align at the equatorial plane of the spindle, whereas in anaphase, the daughter chromosomes (separated chromatids) move towards the opposite poles of the cell.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram below represents an experiment to demonstrate a certain phenomenon in a green plant. Will the level of mercury in the glass tubing rise or fall? Which conducting tissue of the plant does the glass-tubing represent?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 1 mark for correctly stating mercury rises AND that the tubing represents xylem (both required for the mark).
key_points: The mercury level rises due to the suction pull created by transpiration; the glass tubing represents the xylem, the water-conducting tissue
marking_schemes.model_answer: The mercury level rises, due to the suction pull created as water is pulled up and lost through transpiration. The glass tubing represents the xylem tissue, which conducts water in the plant.

marking_schemes.question_text: Define Transpiration.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 1 mark for a correct definition.
key_points: Loss of excess water in the form of vapour from the aerial (surface) parts of a plant, mainly through stomata
marking_schemes.model_answer: Transpiration is the process of loss of excess water in the form of water vapour from the aerial (surface) parts of a plant, mainly through the stomata of leaves.

marking_schemes.question_text: How will the rate of the above process differ if the environment of the plant has: 1. Less humidity 2. High temperature?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 1 mark for correctly stating the effect of both conditions (both required for the mark).
key_points: Less humidity increases the rate of transpiration; high temperature also increases the rate of transpiration
marking_schemes.model_answer: 1. Less humidity in the surrounding air increases the rate of transpiration, since the water vapour concentration gradient between the leaf and air is steeper. 2. High temperature also increases the rate of transpiration, as it increases evaporation of water from leaf surfaces.

marking_schemes.question_text: State any two advantages of transpiration to the plant.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 1 mark for any two correct advantages (both required for the mark).
key_points: Any two valid advantages, e.g. creates suction pull that helps in absorption and upward movement of water and minerals, cools the plant, and helps in gaseous exchange
marking_schemes.model_answer: Advantages of transpiration: (1) It creates a suction pull that helps in the upward movement (absorption and transport) of water and minerals within the plant. (2) It helps keep the plant cool by the evaporative loss of water.
